issues.issue_body:
Follow-up to #1753. These are findings from its final review round (head c345173f0) that are past the round cap. Each one either behaves the same as main or is a wording problem, so none blocks #1753.

- **Other analyses do not apply the linear refusal.** Modal, harmonic, Guyan, Craig–Bampton, time history, Winkler and staged analyses still solve a stiffness that `solve_2d`/`solve_3d` refuse as unresolvable (the soft-inertia beam, `engine/tests/known_issues.rs:616`, `:788`). Main behaves the same; the fix belongs to the later analysis slices.
- **Compensated refinement only runs on some paths.** It runs on 3D sparse and 3D PCG. The 2D sparse, 2D PCG and dense paths still do one triangular solve (`linear.rs:1096`, `:1271`).
- **Refinement scale is floored at 1** (`linear.rs:1439`). It mixes translations, rotations and warping in one scale, so small loads can pass the check early. Use componentwise physical scales.
- **Warping-only torsion cantilever is not frame-invariant** (`engine/tests/metamorphic/stability.rs:562`). The verdict should keep the coupled soft direction in every frame.
- **Misleading refusal text.** `stability.rs:819` reports a conditioning refusal for an indefinite matrix above 64 retained DOFs, where it should say indefinite. `not_positive_definite()` (`linear.rs:782`) names a negative property even when none was found, or when the stability test was skipped.
- **`stability.rs:506`: a strictly negative top eigenvalue is classified Indefinite before the constraint-rounding check.**
- **`docs/solver/stability.md:189` and `:295`.** The rotation-invariance claim needs a qualifier. The `64 b ε max|f|` cutoff should become the direction-specific bound.
- **Nits.** Tests that cannot fail: `three_d_truss_structures.rs:347` and `shell_benchmark.rs:3680`. The audit scripts in `docs/results-changes/1753-*.py` exit 0 even on error.

issues.title: Buckling round-off bound: any constraint couples every DOF, so large forces in one structure can refuse a resolved compression in another
issues.evidence: `F`: separate-member control gives 4971.923398239881, within its existing 1e-6 relative tolerance of the one-element analytical root. Adding an MPC wholly inside the other member makes 2D refuse: compression 1.000e-9 kN, noise 4.441e-8 kN. The constraint restrains an already restrained transverse displacement and cannot change the independent column factor.
issues.issue_body: Follow-up to PR #1745. `coupled_round_off` in engine/src/solver/buckling.rs merges every free DOF into one noise component when the model has any constraint. An MPC wholly inside one disconnected structure then lets that structure's large forces mark a real compression in another structure as round-off, and the analysis is refused. The direction is conservative (a refusal, never a number), but valid analyses are refused. Fix: couple only the DOFs the actual constraints connect, and extend the separate-member control test with a local MPC.

issues.title: 3D free twist about a connector: held by the orphan-rotation guard along a global axis, refused about a skew axis
issues.evidence: `K`: skew connector axis refuses with a connector mechanism; aligned axis still solves with artificial twist zero. The checked-in #1748 test documents exactly this split. No unique free-twist reference is supplied; the observation establishes an orientation-dependent verdict, not a silently wrong unique solution.
issues.issue_body: Follow-up to #1748 / PR #1750. The same free twist about a connector's axis gets a different verdict depending on orientation: along a global axis the existing `orphan_rotation_dofs_3d` guard sees a zero diagonal and holds it with twist 0, about a skew axis the new connector-arm check refuses it. Nothing returns silently, but the verdict is not invariant under rotation, and the nightly rotation relation can report it as a refusal flip. Fix: the guard should stiffen each node's free rotation directions (from the node's rotation block) instead of global DOFs, in all three 3D assemblers, so both orientations get the same verdict. issues.issue_body: Follow-up to #1099 / PR #1746. `refuse_connector_arm_mechanism_2d` counts a node tied by a constraint as held, but a constraint can carry the mechanism without restraining it (for example a coincident dummy node rigid-linked to node 2). Such models skip the check and behave as on main before #1746. The proper check reads the stiffness after the constraint transform in `solve_constrained_2d`. Reproducer first, then the fix.
issue_comments: Also 3D: `refuse_connector_arm_mechanism_3d` (PR #1750, #1748) leaves out nodes of constraints that tie a rotation, including rigid-link masters and diaphragm nodes. The fix for both is the same: run the check on the stiffness after the constraint transform.

issues.title: 3D: a rotation 1e12 softer than another axis at the same node is locked by the orphan spring
issues.evidence: `F`, `R`: regular and prepared return ry(2) = 0.024999999999999988 rad versus the issue’s PL²/(2EI) = 0.025 rad; relative error about 5.6e-16, within the existing regression’s 1e-6 tolerance. The existing regression and its 1e-4-inertia control pass.
issues.issue_body:
Found while landing #1428 (the #1367 fix). #1428 judges a rotation as an orphan against the stiffest rotation **at its own node**, no longer against the whole model. When one rotational axis at a node is more than 1e12 softer than another axis at that same node, the soft axis is still taken for an orphan and held by the artificial spring.

Reproducer (on #1428's head): a 3D cantilever of length 1, E = 200000 MPa, A = 0.01, Iy = 1e-10, Iz = 1e3, J = 1e3, fixed at node 1, tip load fz = -1e-3 kN at node 2.
- `solve_3d` gives ry(2) = 2.08e-6 rad. The exact value is PL²/(2EI) = 2.5e-2 rad, so the result is wrong by four orders of magnitude.
- The only diagnostic is NUM-INVARIANCE. The ORPHAN-SOFT-ROTATION warning (an artificially held DOF that moves) fires on it on prepared static solves.
- With Iy = 1e-4 the result is exact (2.5e-8).

The fix would be an orphan test that does not compare across axes, for example the DOF's diagonal against its own element contributions.

issues.title: 2D limit analysis: self-stress rank cutoff loses redistribution when capacities differ by about 1e9 (12 instead of 16, conservative)
issues.evidence: `F`: raw limit_analysis_2d returns lambda = lambda_upper = 11.999999999999998 versus reference 16 (relative deficit 0.25). Confirmation is explicitly Contradicted with certified bounds [15.999999984, 16]. The rank loss remains, but it is detected; the public solve_plastic_2d is withheld by PL-2D-INVARIANCE. No silent public result/advisory claim.
issues.issue_body:
Follow-up from #1447 (#758), Codex review rounds 1 and 3.

`engine/src/solver/plastic_limit.rs` cuts the self-stress basis at `1e-9 * top`, where `top` is the largest weighted field (weights 1/Mp, 1/Np). When member capacities differ by about 10⁹ or more, the weaker members' fields fall below the cut and their redistribution is lost.

Reproduction: two disconnected fixed-fixed beams, L = 1, same section, Mp = 1 and 10¹⁰, UDL 10⁻¹² and 10¹⁰. The limit analysis returns λ = 12 (first yield, 12Mp/qL²); the right value is 16 (16Mp/qL²).

This is conservative (too low), and `lambda_upper` is then not an upper bound.

Tried in #1447 and reverted: normalising each field before the cut (equilibration). It fixes this case but makes fuzz_rich_2d/20840 depend on units: λ is 0.7016 in some unit systems and 0.2750 in others, because a near-dependent field comes and goes, which is unconservative. The fix needs a rank decision that is both scale-equilibrated and unit-invariant, or one that refuses when the rank is unresolved. The test to add is the two-beam absolute reference above.
issue_comments:
Codex (round 11 on #1447 at 6a45d08b62) found the same kind of problem from a different direction. Take the shallow-arch construction with rise = 1e-10 and Np = Mp/rise. The analytical factor stays near 0.2, but the self-stress mode that provides it falls below both the norm cutoff (`nk > 1e-9·top`) and the per-component chop (1e-9·scale) in `engine/src/solver/plastic_limit.rs`. The chop can also leave a basis field that is out of equilibrium by about 1e-9 relative.

With #1447, a lost mode lowers the LP factor (conservative), and the exact rational certificate then reports it as contradicted or bracketed rather than exact. The result is shown as unconfirmed, not passed silently. What should change: keep independent modes with per-mode normalization, check the retained basis for equilibrium, and refuse when conditioning prevents that check.

issues.title: 2D: refuse a nodal moment on an artificial rotational DOF, as 3D does
issues.evidence: `F`: the issue explicitly says this was not a live bug after #1428. Its requested artificial-rotation probe (the exact #1437 model with the spring zeroed) refuses a nodal moment in regular, prepared, constrained and one-stage paths. No formerly silent wrong result reproduced.
issues.issue_body:
Defence in depth after #1428 (fix for #1367/#1437).

3D refuses a nodal moment applied on an artificial DOF before certifying. 2D only fails such a DOF when its rotation exceeds 100 rad, which is how #1437's 75 rad got through. With #1428 the 2D orphan threshold is exactly zero, so this is not a live bug, but 2D should match 3D: add the refusal in `PreparedStatic2D::solve_loads_by_path` and the constrained 2D path, with a regression test that loads an artificial rotational DOF.

Also unchecked: `engine/src/.../staged.rs` builds its own artificial DOFs (around line 569) and #1428 does not touch it. Audit it for the same threshold.
issue_comments: Also found while checking #1428 (head d85bfce69): a 3D node with all rotations released and springs krx = kry = 1, krz = 1e-13 is refused with "Nodal moment at node 2 is not supported". It is safe, but the message is misleading, because the node does have a rotational spring. #1428's per-node rule still treats the 1e-13 rotation as stiffness-free next to the stiffer ones. Either reword the refusal or stop treating a rotation with its own spring support as stiffness-free.
